Thanks — I pulled traces and queue snapshots. Preliminary findings below (traces attached: request-trace-20260607.log).

Short summary:
- Root cause appears to be a misconfiguration in the rate-limit/quota routing rules created during last week's burst-credit rollout. A new priority_silo routing rule was added but the time-window buckets overlap with the tenant-level quota window. When Medivance's burst window opened, requests were incorrectly routed into the shared low-priority pool (shared-low-1) instead of the high-priority pool (mdv-dedicated-1). That pool was already near capacity, which triggered immediate 429/503 rejections and elevated latency as retries compounded.

Evidence:
- Trace abc123 shows 73% of MDV traffic routed to shared-low-1 between 07:54-08:02 PT.
- The rate limiter evaluated window_start and priority tags in the wrong precedence order due to an earlier patch that changed evaluation order for overlapping windows.

Immediate actions taken (09:05 PT):
1) Suspended the new priority_silo rule (hotfix) so routing falls back to the canonical tenant mapping.
2) Temporarily increased Medivance burst credits by 3x for 30 minutes to drain backlog.
3) Enabled safety-valve override for high-latency requests to allow short-lived rate bursts while we verify correctness.

Next steps (owner in parentheses):
- Run a full audit of routing precedence and add unit tests for overlapping-window semantics (Monica).
- Coordinate a post-mortem and communicate SLA impact and credits to the customer (Evelyn).
- Consider a longer-term config change to eliminate overlapping buckets or to add explicit non-overlapping precedence (Karthik).

Attachments: request-trace-20260607.log, proposed-mitigation-playbook.md

Team — thank you. Final update for execs and next steps: 

Status: mitigated (traffic normalized by 18:02 PT after hotfix + burst credit lift). Error rate peaked at 8.2% and returned to <0.5% within 45 minutes. Median latency back to ~130ms.

Root cause (short): an overlapping priority_silo time-window rule (deployed as part of last week's burst-credit rollout) that had higher evaluation precedence than tenant canonical mapping. The changed precedence caused requests to be routed to a lower-capacity pool, producing rejections and amplified latency under load.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Suspended offending priority rule (Monica)
- Temporary burst-credit increase for MDV-2391 while we drained queues (Ops)
- Safety-valve override enabled for high-latency requests

Follow-up actions (owners/timelines):
- Full config rollback and test harness for overlapping windows (Monica) — in progress, ETA 24h
- Post-mortem with timeline, customer impact calc, and proposed credits (Evelyn) — draft by EOD tomorrow
- Product change to ban overlapping windows or to enforce explicit precedence rules (Karthik & Eng) — proposal in 2 weeks

Customer comms: Evelyn, please send a concise incident note to Michael and Procurement that includes the timeline and proposed good-faith credit. If MDV asks for an expedited credit approval, route to revenue ops with cc to me.

Thanks again for rapid response. Let's capture lessons learned in the post-mortem so this doesn't recur.
